children.text: @praṇipatya %ekam anekam kam satyām devatām param brahma/
children.translated_text: Having paid homage to <s>Brahman</s>, who is the one, the many, and the true supreme deity,
<s>Āryabhaṭa</s> sets forth three [subjects]: mathematics, reckoning of time, and the celestial sphere.

The consonant-letters of the varga groups [represent values] in the varga [square] places; the consonant-letters of the avarga groups in the avarga [non-square] places; from ka [onward], ṅa and ma are ya;
kha [represents] two nines; the vowels [represent] nine [successive powers] in the varga and avarga places, and nine in the final varga place.
The revolutions of the Sun and stars in a <s>yuga</s> (age) are [encoded as] khyughṛ; the Moon's [revolutions] are cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ; the ascending node's are ku ṅiśibuṇḷṣkhṛ, retrograde;
Saturn's are ḍhuṅvighva; Jupiter's are khricyubha; Mars's are bhadlijhnukhṛ; [these are] Venus, Mercury, and the [revolutions] of Saturn [etc.].
The Moon's apogee [revolutions are] rjuṣkhidha; Mercury's are suguśithṛna; Venus's are jaṣabikhuchṛ; the remainder [is] the Sun's;
buphinaca — the nodes move in reverse; [measured] from the Mercury-day [Wednesday], from the rise of the Sun at <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: ka-ahas manavas $ḍha manu-yugās $śkha gatās te ca manu-yugās $chnā ca/
children.translated_text: The days of a <s>Manu</s>'s [period are encoded as] ka; [number of] days, <s>Manus</s>; [<s>Manu</s>-]<s>yugas</s> [are encoded as] ḍha; those <s>Manu</s>-<s>yugas</s> that have passed and the <s>Manu</s>-<s>yugas</s> are chnā; and

children.text: kalpa-ādes yuga-#pādās $ga ca guru-divasāt ca bhāratāt pūrvam//
children.translated_text: <s>yuga</s>-quarters from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> [are encoded as] ga; and before the <s>Bhārata</s> [war] from the day of Jupiter.
The Moon's [orbit in] <s>rāśis</s> (zodiacal signs) [is encoded as] ṭha; those in degrees, minutes, and <s>yojanas</s> [are] yavaña times the [relevant] quantities;

children.text: prāṇena @eti kalām bham kha-yuga-aṃśe graha-javas bha-$va-aṃśe arkas//
children.translated_text: in one <s>prāṇa</s> (respiration) [the celestial sphere] moves one minute; the planetary velocity [is expressed] in the kha-<s>yuga</s> part of the sky, and the Sun's in the bha-va part.
A <s>yojana</s> for a person is [encoded as] ṣi; the earth's diameter is ñilā; the [diameters] of the Sun and Moon are ghriñā and giṇa; [that of] <s>Meru</s> is ka;
Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and Mars have [diameters of] the Moon's ṅa, ña, ṇa, na, and ma parts, [all] measured as equal to the Sun.
The maximum declination of the [ecliptic from the equator is encoded as] bha; the planetary [orbital] inclinations from the ecliptic — the Moon's deviation from the ecliptic is jha and a half;
Saturn, Jupiter, Mars [have inclinations of] kha, ka, ga and a half; Venus and Mercury [have] kha and sca degrees, gha cubits, and nā [respectively].
Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, having traversed [the encoded] na, va, rā, ṣa, ha degrees, [reach] the first nodes;
and likewise for those of the Sun — the <s>manda</s> (slow) apogees are dvā, ñakhi, sā, hdā, hlya, khicya.
Jha and a half [gives] the <s>manda</s> epicycle; for the Moon: cha, ga, cha, gha, ḍha, cha, jha — from those stated;
jhā, gḍa, glā, rdha, dḍa likewise for the <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> (fast) apogees of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury.
From the <s>manda</s> [apogee]: ṅa, kha, da, ja, ḍā [are the epicycle circumferences] — retrograde planets in the second and fourth quadrants;
from the apogee the <s>śīghra</s> [epicycles are] jā, ṇa, kla, chla, jhna; giyiṅaśa [encode] the final orbits of the Earth, Wind, and Sky.
Makhi, bhaki, phakhi, dhakhi, ṇakhi, ñakhi, ṅakhi, hasjha, skaki, kiṣga, śghaki, kighva,
ghlaki, kigra, hakya, dhaki, kica, sga, jhaśa, ṅva, kla, pta, pha, cha — [these are the] half-chord [R-sine] differences.
This <s>sūtra</s> of the ten <s>gītikā</s> verses — having understood the motions of the earth and planets within the cage of stars,
one who knows the revolution of the planets and stars goes, having pierced through, to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
Having paid homage to <s>Brahmā</s>, the Earth, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, [and the constellation] Koṇa and the stars,

children.text: āryabhaṭas tu iha @nigadati kusuma-pure abhyarcitam jñānam//
children.translated_text: <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> here sets forth the knowledge honored in <s>Kusumapura</s> (Pāṭaliputra).
One, ten, hundred, thousand, <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand), <s>niyuta</s> (hundred thousand), likewise <s>prayuta</s> (million),
<s>koṭi</s> (ten million), <s>arbuda</s> (hundred million), and <s>vṛnda</s> (billion) — from place to place, each is ten times [the previous].

children.text: vargas sama-%catur-aśras phalam ca sadṛśa-%dvayasya saṃvargas/
children.translated_text: A square is an equilateral quadrilateral; its area is the product of two equal [sides];
a cube is the product of three equals, and it is also a twelve-edged [solid].
One should always divide the non-square [place] by twice the square root;

children.text: vargāt varge śuddhe labdham sthāna-antare mūlam//
children.translated_text: the quotient, after subtracting the square from the square [place], is the root in the next place.
One should divide the second non-cube [place] by three times the square of the cube root;
the square [of the quotient] multiplied by three times the previous [root] should be subtracted from the first [non-cube place], and the cube from the cube [place].
The area of a triangle is the product of half the base and the perpendicular height;
half the product of that [area] and the vertical [height] is the volume of a six-edged [solid] (triangular prism).
Half the circumference multiplied by half the diameter is the area of a circle;
that [area] multiplied by its own square root is the exact volume of a sphere.
The two sides, multiplied by the length, divided by their sum, give the <s>sva-pāta-lekha</s> (perpendicular segments);
the area of a trapezoid should be known as the product of half the sum of the widths multiplied by the length.
Having determined the sides of all plane figures, the area is their product;
the chord of one-sixth of the circumference is equal to half the diameter.
One hundred and four multiplied by eight, and sixty-two thousands,
is the approximate circumference of a circle of diameter twenty thousand.
One should divide the quarter of the circumference of a circle equally from the triangle and quadrilateral;
the half-chords of equal arcs [are computed] as desired within the semi-diameter.
The second half-chord [is] the first half-chord of the arc diminished by the amount by which it is reduced;
the remainders are [each] diminished by those respective parts of the first half-chord.

children.text: vṛttam bhrameṇa sādhyam ca %catur-bhujam ca karṇābhyām/
children.translated_text: A circle [is to be verified] by rotation, and a quadrilateral by its diagonals;

children.text: sādhyā jalena sama-bhūs adhas-ūrdhvam lambakena eva//
children.translated_text: a level surface [is to be verified] with water; a vertical [is verified] with a plumb-line.
Having added the square of the height of the <s>śaṅku</s> (gnomon) to the square of the shadow,
the square root of that is the semi-diameter of its own circle (the hypotenuse).
The product of the gnomon and the distance between the gnomon and the [light source], divided by the difference of the gnomon and the [light source],

children.text: yat labdham sā chāyā jñeyā śaṅkos sva-mūlāt hi//
children.translated_text: the quotient is the shadow — it should be known from the base of the gnomon.
The distance between the tips of the shadows multiplied by the shadow, divided by the difference [of the shadows], is the <s>koṭi</s> (upright);
the <s>koṭi</s> multiplied by the gnomon and divided by the shadow gives the <s>bhujā</s> (base).

children.text: yas ca eva bhujā-vargas koṭī-vargas ca karṇa-vargas sas/
children.translated_text: The square of the <s>bhujā</s> (base) and the square of the <s>koṭi</s> (upright) [together] equal the square of the <s>karṇa</s> (hypotenuse);
in a circle, the product of the arrows [sagitta] is the square of the half-chord — that indeed [applies to] both arcs.
The two circles diminished by the overlap, each multiplied by the overlap, should be divided separately;
the quotients from the sum diminished by the overlap are the two arrows of intersection, reciprocally.

children.text: iṣṭam vi-%ekam dalitam sa-pūrvam uttara-guṇam sa-mukham madhyam/
children.translated_text: The desired [term number] minus one, halved, plus the preceding [terms], multiplied by the common difference, plus the first [term], gives the middle [term];

children.text: iṣṭa-guṇitam iṣṭa-dhanam tu atha vā ādi-antam pada-%ardha-hatam//
children.translated_text: the desired [number of terms] multiplied by the middle [term] gives the desired sum; or [alternatively], the sum of the first and last [terms] multiplied by half the number of terms.
The number of terms [is found from]: the square root of the sum multiplied by eight times the common difference, plus the square of the difference of twice the first term and the common difference,
minus twice the first term, divided by the common difference, plus one, halved.
Of a series increasing by one from the first term, the product of three [consecutive terms] beginning with one more than the number of terms,
divided by six, is the sum of the series of solids; plus the cube of [one more than] the number of terms, minus the root.
The sixth part of the product of three consecutive terms beginning with one, [together with] the one-more-than-the-number-of-terms,
is the solid sum of squares; the square sum, and the solid sum of cubes also [follow from this].
From the square of the sum, one should subtract the sum of the squares;
half of that is the product-sum (<s>guṇakāra-saṃvarga</s>).
The square root of: the product multiplied by twice the square, plus the square of the difference of the two,
plus and minus the difference, divided by two — [gives] the two factors.
The principal with interest, multiplied by the time and the rate, plus the square of half the principal,
the square root of that, minus half the principal, divided by the time, gives the interest on one's own principal.
Having multiplied the result-quantity by the desire-quantity in the rule of three,
the quotient obtained by dividing by the measure-quantity — that will be the fruit of the desire.
The denominators are mutually multiplied in the case of multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction of fractions;
the numerator multiplied by the [other's] denominator, with the [other] denominator — that mutual [operation] is reduction to a common denominator.
Multipliers become divisors, and divisors become multipliers;

children.text: yas kṣepas sas apacayas apacayas kṣepas ca viparīte//
children.translated_text: what is additive becomes subtractive, and what is subtractive becomes additive, in the inverse [operation].
The sum decreased by [successive] amounts, the number-of-terms wealth accumulated separately,

children.text: vi-%ekena padena hṛtam sarva-dhanam tat @bhavati evam//
children.translated_text: divided by the number of terms minus one — that becomes the total wealth, in this manner.
One should divide the difference in coins of two persons by the difference in their gems;
the quotient is the price of a gem, if the wealth produced is equal.
In the case of meeting, [when traveling] in opposite directions, [divide] by the sum of speeds; in the same direction by two;
the quotient from the difference of speeds gives the two meeting times — past and future.
One should divide the remainder of the greater by the remainder of the lesser [divisor];
the mutual remainders are multiplied by a chosen number and added to the difference of remainders.
The result multiplied below and above, added to the last, divided by the lesser-remainder's divisor — the residue,
multiplied by the greater-remainder's divisor, added to the greater remainder, [divided by the product] of the two divisors, gives the two-divisor remainder.

body.translated_text: Chapter on the Reckoning of Time

children.translated_text: A year has twelve months; a month has thirty days;
a day has sixty <s>nāḍīs</s>; and a <s>nāḍī</s> has sixty <s>vināḍikās</s>.

children.text: guru-akṣarāṇi %ṣaṣṭis vināḍikā ārkṣī %ṣaṭ eva vā prāṇās/
children.translated_text: A <s>vināḍikā</s> has sixty heavy syllables; a <s>sidereal</s> [<s>vināḍikā</s>] has six <s>prāṇas</s> (respirations);
thus is the division of time; and the division of space is likewise from the stellar revolutions.
The differences of the revolutions of any two are the [number of] conjunctions [of those two] in a <s>yuga</s>;
The revolutions of the Sun, Moon, and asterisms combined give the <s>vyatīpātas</s> (solsticial conjunctions).
The revolutions of their own apogees diminished by their own planetary revolutions give the revolutions of their apogee-perigee cycles;
the revolutions of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) multiplied by twelve, starting from <s>Aśvayuja</s>, give the years of <s>Guru</s>.
The revolutions of the Sun are solar years; the conjunctions of the Sun and Moon are lunar months;

children.text: ravi-bhū-yogās divasās bha-āvartās ca api nākṣatrās//
children.translated_text: the conjunctions of the Sun and Earth are civil days; the rotations of the asterisms are also sidereal days.

children.text: adhimāsakās yuge te ravi-māsebhyas adhikās tu ye cāndrās/
children.translated_text: The intercalary months in a <s>yuga</s> (age) are those lunar months that exceed the solar months;
the lunar days should be known; those less than the civil days are the omitted <s>tithis</s> (lunar days).

children.text: ravi-varṣam mānuṣyam tat api triṃśat-guṇam @bhavati pitryam/
children.translated_text: The solar year is the human year; that multiplied by thirty becomes a year of the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors);
the year of the <s>pitṛs</s> multiplied by twelve is declared to be the divine year.
A thousand divine years multiplied by twelve is the common planetary <s>yuga</s>;
one thousand and eight planetary <s>yugas</s> constitute a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: utsarpiṇī yuga-%ardham paścāt apasarpiṇī yuga-%ardham ca/
children.translated_text: The ascending half-cycle (<s>utsarpiṇī</s>) constitutes half a <s>yuga</s>, and afterward the descending half-cycle (<s>apasarpiṇī</s>) the other half;

children.text: madhye yugasya suṣamā ādau ante duṣṣamā indu-uccāt//
children.translated_text: in the middle of the <s>yuga</s> is the period of happiness (<s>suṣamā</s>), at the beginning and end the period of unhappiness (<s>duṣṣamā</s>), reckoned from the apogee of the Moon.
When sixty times sixty years and three quarter-<s>yugas</s> had elapsed,

children.text: %tri-adhikā %viṃśatis abdās tadā iha mama janmanas atītās//
children.translated_text: twenty-three years had then passed since my birth here.
The <s>yuga</s>, the year, the month, and the day commence simultaneously from the beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>;
this time, without beginning or end, is measured by the planetary asterisms in the field of the zodiac.
In sixty solar years, the planets complete the circumference of their asterisms,
revolving equally in their own orbits through the circumference of the sky by divine measure.

children.text: maṇḍalam alpam adhastāt kālena alpena @pūrayati candras/
children.translated_text: The Moon, situated below in a small orbit, completes it in a short time;

children.text: upariṣṭāt sarveṣām mahat ca mahatā śanaiścārī//
children.translated_text: situated above all, <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) completes a great orbit in a long time.

children.text: alpe hi maṇḍale alpā mahati mahāntas ca rāśayas jñeyās/
children.translated_text: In a small orbit, the signs are to be known as small; in a great orbit, they are great;

children.text: aṃśās kalās tathā evam vibhāga-tulyās sva-kakṣyāsu//
children.translated_text: likewise the degrees and minutes are equal divisions proportional in their own orbits.
Below the asterisms are <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Suraguru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), <s>Arka</s> (Sun), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Candra</s> (Moon);

children.text: eṣām adhas ca bhūmis medhī-bhūtā kha-madhya-sthā//
children.translated_text: below these is the Earth, situated in the center of space, like the axis of a wheel.
These seven are the lords of the <s>horās</s> (hours), beginning with <s>Śanaiścara</s> and successively faster;
the fourth from each in the order of speed becomes the lord of the day, starting from sunrise.
All planets revolve by their own motion in their orbit-eccentric circles;

children.text: manda-uccāt anulomam pratilomam ca eva śīghra-uccāt//
children.translated_text: direct from the <s>manda-ucca</s> (apogee of slow inequality), and retrograde from the <s>śīghra-ucca</s> (apogee of fast inequality).
The eccentric circle of each is equal to its own orbit;
the center of the eccentric circle is displaced from the center of the solid Earth.
The distance between the eccentric and the Earth is the semi-diameter of the apogee-perigee circle;
the planets revolve thus on the circumference of that circle, from their mean motion.
A planet that is fast from its apogee has retrograde motion in its own circle and orbit,
while a planet that has direct motion in the circle becomes slow.
The circles from the <s>manda</s> (slow) [apogee] are direct; from the <s>śīghra</s> (fast) [apogee], they are retrograde;
a planet is mean when at the junction of its own circle and the orbit.
Subtractive, additive, additive, and subtractive corrections arise from the <s>manda-ucca</s>; reversed from the <s>śīghra-ucca</s>;
for <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), from the <s>manda</s>, the first half is subtractive and the second additive.

children.text: manda-uccāt śīghra-uccāt %ardham ṛṇam dhanam graheṣu mandeṣu/
children.translated_text: From the <s>manda-ucca</s> and from the <s>śīghra-ucca</s>, the first half is subtractive and the second additive for the slow-moving planets;

children.text: manda-uccāt sphuṭa-madhyās śīghra-uccāt ca sphuṭās jñeyās//
children.translated_text: from the <s>manda-ucca</s>, the true-mean positions are obtained; from the <s>śīghra-ucca</s>, the true positions are to be known.
From the <s>śīghra-ucca</s>, half the correction, subtractive or additive, should be applied to the <s>manda-ucca</s>;

children.text: sphuṭa-madhyau tu bhṛgu-budhau siddhāt mandāt sphuṭau @bhavatas//
children.translated_text: the true-mean positions of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) become true when corrected for the <s>manda</s>.
The product of the distance between the Earth and a planet and its own hypotenuse, divided by the semi-diameter,
gives the velocity of the planet in the orbit; this applies at the <s>manda</s> perigee and apogee.
From <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) to the end of <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo), the ecliptic has gone north by half its declination equally;
from <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) to the end of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces), the remaining half has gone south.
The star-planets, the Moon, and the nodes revolve constantly on the ecliptic, as does the Sun;

children.text: arkāt ca maṇḍala-%ardhe @bhramati hi tasmin kṣiti-chāyā//
children.translated_text: at half an orbit from the Sun, the shadow of the Earth revolves on that same ecliptic.
The Moon, from the node, travels north and south of the ecliptic;

children.text: kuja-guru-koṇās ca evam śīghra-uccena api budha-śukrau//
children.translated_text: likewise <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Koṇa</s> (Saturn), and also <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) by their <s>śīghra-ucca</s>.
The Moon, when at a distance of twelve degrees from the Sun, uneclipsed, is visible;
<s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) at nine degrees, and from that, each successively two more—thus the fainter ones.
Half the spheres of the Earth, planets, and asterisms are darkened by their own shadow;
the other halves, according to their nature, shine facing the Sun.
In the middle of the sphere of asterisms, encircled by orbits, situated in the center of space,
the sphere of the Earth is round on all sides, composed of earth, water, fire, and air.
Just as the core of a <s>kadamba</s> flower is densely packed with blossoms on all sides,

children.text: tad-vat hi sarva-sattvais jala-jais sthala-jais ca bhū-golas//
children.translated_text: so too the sphere of the Earth is covered on all sides by all living beings, born in water and on land.
In a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, the Earth's surface increases by one <s>yojana</s> upward;
in a night equal to the day, the earth that was accumulated decreases [by the same amount].
Just as one standing in a boat moving forward sees stationary objects moving backward,
so at <s>Laṅkā</s>, the stationary asterisms appear to move uniformly westward.
Constantly impelled by the <s>pravaha</s> wind, the cause of rising and setting,
the sphere of asterisms with the planets revolves, moving uniformly westward at <s>Laṅkā</s>.
<s>Meru</s> is one <s>yojana</s> in extent, luminous, surrounded by the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalaya) mountains;
in the middle of the <s>Nandana</s> garden, it is made of jewels, round on all sides.

children.text: svar-merū sthala-madhye narakas baḍavā-mukham ca jala-madhye/
children.translated_text: The celestial <s>Meru</s> is in the middle of the land, and the submarine fire (<s>Baḍavāmukha</s>) is in the middle of the water;
the gods and the demons each consider the other to be situated below, certainly.

children.text: udayas yas laṅkāyām sas astamayas savitur eva siddha-pure/
children.translated_text: The rising at <s>Laṅkā</s> is the setting of the Sun at <s>Siddhapura</s>;
noon at <s>Yamakoṭi</s> is midnight in the land of <s>Romaka</s>.
<s>Laṅkā</s> is at the midpoint of land and water, at one-quarter of the Earth's circumference;
<s>Ujjayinī</s> is due north of <s>Laṅkā</s> at one-quarter of that distance.

children.text: bhū-vyāsa-%ardhena ūnam dṛśyam deśāt samāt bha-gola-%ardham/
children.translated_text: From a place on the equator, half the celestial sphere minus the Earth's semi-diameter is visible;
half is hidden by the Earth, and the Earth's semi-diameter adds to that.
The gods situated at <s>Meru</s> in the north see half the celestial sphere revolving to the right;
the <s>pretas</s> (departed spirits) at the submarine fire in the south see the other half revolving to the left.

children.text: ravi-varṣa-%ardham devās @paśyanti uditam ravim tathā pretās/
children.translated_text: The gods see the Sun risen for half a solar year, and so too do the <s>pretas</s>;

children.text: śaśi-māsa-%ardham pitaras śaśi-gās ku-dina-%ardham iha manu-jās//
children.translated_text: the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) on the Moon see it for half a lunar month; humans here see it for half a civil day.

children.text: pūrva-aparam adhas-ūrdhvam maṇḍalam atha dakṣiṇa-uttaram ca eva/
children.translated_text: The east-west and the below-above circles, and also the south-north circle—
the horizon circle is on the side of the Earth, where the rising and setting of the asterisms occur.

children.text: pūrva-apara-diś-lagnam kṣiti-jāt akṣa-agrayos ca lagnam yat/
children.translated_text: That which intersects the east-west cardinal points and the two poles of the horizon
is the meridian circle (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>), where the increase and decrease of day and night occur.

children.text: pūrva-apara-diś-rekhā adhas ca ūrdhvā dakṣiṇa-uttara-sthā ca/
children.translated_text: The east-west line, the below-above line, and the south-north line—
the intersection of these is where the observer is, at whatever place.

children.text: ūrdhvam adhastāt draṣṭur jñeyam dṛś-maṇḍalam graha-abhimukham/
children.translated_text: The visible hemisphere, facing the planets, should be known above and below the observer;
the circle of ecliptic latitude, intersecting the east point, is three signs less.

children.text: kāṣṭha-mayam sama-vṛttam samantatas sama-gurum laghum golam/
children.translated_text: A sphere made of wood, perfectly round, equally weighted on all sides, and light—
one should rotate it with mercury, oil, and water, and by one's own ingenuity, in accordance with time.
On the visible hemisphere of the sphere, one should construct half the celestial sphere with half-chords;
the equinoctial sine, the latitude-sine—the perpendicular is the complementary sine of the latter.
Subtracting the square of the desired declination from the square of the semi-diameter, the square root
gives, north or south of the equator, half the diameter of the day-circle.
The desired sine multiplied by half the diameter of the day-circle, the final [arc],
divided by half of the day-circle, gives the result: the rising-arc from <s>Laṅkā</s> measured from <s>Aja</s> (Aries).
The latitude-sine multiplied by the desired declination, divided by the co-latitude,
gives the <s>kṣitijā</s> (horizon-sine) on the day-circle—the ascensional difference for day and night.
A quadrant of the circle rises in a quarter of a day diminished by half the ascensional difference

children.text: %prathamas antyas ca atha anyau tad-sahitena krama-utkramaśas//
children.translated_text: for the first and last [quadrants], and for the other two, increased by it, in direct and reverse order.
The desired sine of the day-circle from the horizon, multiplied by the co-latitude,
divided by the semi-diameter, gives the gnomon for the elapsed and remaining parts of the day.
The desired gnomon multiplied by the equinoctial sine, divided by its own co-latitude,
gives the tip of the solar gnomon south of the east-west line of rising and setting.
The sine of the maximum declination, multiplied by the desired half-sine, should then be divided;

children.text: jyā lambakena labdhā arka-agrā pūrva-apare kṣiti-je//
children.translated_text: the sine [so obtained], divided by the co-latitude (<s>lambaka</s>), gives the solar amplitude (<s>arkāgrā</s>) on the east-west horizon line.
If that is less than the equinoctial shadow-sine, then multiplied by the equinoctial north co-latitude,
divided by the equinoctial sine, the result is the gnomon on the east-west [line].

children.text: kṣiti-jāt unnata-bhāgānām yā jyā sā paras @bhavet śaṅkus/
children.translated_text: The sine of the degrees of elevation above the horizon — that becomes the other gnomon;

children.text: madhyāt nata-bhāga-jyā chāyā śaṅkos tu tasya eva//
children.translated_text: the sine of the degrees of depression from the meridian is the shadow of that same gnomon.
In the product of the meridian sine and the sine of rising, divided by the semi-diameter,
the square root of the difference of the squares of that and the meridian sine is the own latitude-displacement (<s>svadṛkkṣepa</s>).
The square root of the difference between the squares of the latitude-displacement and the visual displacement is the own visual motion, due to the earth;
at the horizon, the own visual shadow is the semi-diameter of the earth from the middle of the sky.
The sine of the latitude multiplied by the sine of the celestial latitude, divided by the co-latitude, becomes subtractive when [the body is] to the north;

children.text: udaye dhanam astamaye dakṣiṇa-ge dhanam ṛṇam candre//
children.translated_text: additive at rising and subtractive at setting; additive for the Moon when [it is] to the south, subtractive [when to the north].
The product of the celestial latitude and the declination, [being] the versed sine, divided by the square of the semi-diameter —

children.text: udac-ṛṇa-dhanam udac-ayane dakṣiṇa-ge dhanam ṛṇam yāmye//
children.translated_text: subtractive for the north in the northern solstice; additive for the south, subtractive in the southern [solstice].

children.text: candras jalam arkas agnis mṛd-bhū-chāyā api yā tamas tat hi/
children.translated_text: The Moon is water; the Sun is fire; the earth — and its shadow too — that indeed is darkness;

children.text: @chādayati śaśī sūryam śaśinam mahatī ca bhū-chāyā//
children.translated_text: the Moon obscures the Sun, and the great shadow of the earth [obscures] the Moon.
At the end of the true lunar month, when the Moon, near the node, enters [the path of] the Sun,
and [enters] the shadow of the earth at the end of the half-month — then, more or less, is the middle of the eclipse.
The distance between the earth and the Sun, multiplied by the earth and divided by the difference between the Sun and the earth —
gives the length of the earth's shadow; the result [is measured] from the diameter of the earth-globe.
The distance between the tip of the shadow and the Moon, multiplied by the earth's diameter,
divided by the earth's shadow — one should know this as the diameter of the shadow [at the Moon's distance].
From the square of the half-sum of that and the Moon [diameters], the square of the Moon's celestial latitude should be subtracted;
the square root of this is the half-duration (<s>sthityardha</s>) [of the eclipse], to be known from the daily motion of the Moon and Sun.
The half of the shadow-[diameter] minus the half of the Moon's diameter — the square of that,
minus the square of the celestial latitude — the square root of the remainder is the half of the total phase (<s>vimardārdha</s>).
Subtracting from the celestial latitude the half of the shadow's diameter minus the half of the Moon's diameter,

children.text: vikṣepāt yat śeṣam na @gṛhyate tat śaśāṅkasya//
children.translated_text: the remainder — that [portion] of the Moon is not eclipsed.
From the half-duration plus the square of the celestial latitude, subtracting the desired [time], the square root
should be subtracted from the half-contact — the remainder is the eclipse magnitude at that time.
The latitude multiplied by the midday versed sine, from the south, divided by the semi-diameter, gives the direction;
and from the half-duration of the Sun and Moon, with three signs added to the longitude, [determines] the first contact.
At the end of a partial eclipse the Moon is smoky; in a partial eclipse it becomes black;
in a total eclipse it is tawny, and dark-coppery in the middle of the shadow.
When the circumferences of the Sun and Moon coincide, one-eighth of the Sun's [disc] becomes invisible,
because of the luminous nature of the Sun and because the circumference of the Moon is very transparent and thin.
The Sun illuminates [the Moon] from the conjunction of the earth and Sun; and [one should] calculate the Moon from the conjunction of the Sun and Moon;
from the conjunction of the Moon with the stars and planets, likewise all the stars and planets [are illuminated].
From the ocean of true and false knowledge, extracted by the grace of <s>Brahmā</s>,
the supreme gem of true knowledge has been brought up by me through the boat of my own intellect.

children.text: āryabhaṭīyam nāmnā pūrvam svāyambhuavam sadā nityam/
children.translated_text: The <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s> by name, formerly the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> (of Brahmā), eternal and everlasting —
whoever makes a counterfeit of it brings about the destruction of his own merit and lifespan.
